entries.notes: F$ID/F$Time/F$CmpNam per 68k/syscall-reference.md. F$ID's d1=group.user(packed,0 here)/d2=priority(128, the shell-forked default) are the doc-settled register mapping -- the file's own inline comment guessed the opposite order before that was confirmed live. The F$Time printed digits are NOT asserted: printnum (this file's own decimal-print helper) corrupts values above 65535 via an unguarded 16-bit DIVU, and F$Time's packed time value routinely exceeds that -- a real bug in the 2026-07-18 test helper, not in os9exec, discovered while authoring this oracle. Only the PASS/FAIL branch taken is checked.

os9fork()'s bare (no leading /) modname argument resolves the way Shell does, via the module directory (F$Load-resident) -- os9-clib-reference.md's previously-untested case. childprg68k exits F$Exit(77), which the C program's wait() confirms echoed back exactly.

A single process holding both a writer (UPDATE) and reader (READ) path on the same file: the reader catching up while its own process's writer path is open is refused as E_DEADLK (254), not silently allowed to hang or mis-report EOF -- file-managers.md's Record Locking design intent.

Wraps the already-complete E$BMode repro script (this test wraps the SCRIPT's own exit code / PASS marker, not a fresh oracle) -- writing to a file opened read-only, and reading one opened write-only, both return E$BMode (203).

A host-native directory must report its own FD position in SS_Opt's PD_FD, so that a ..-walking getwd()/getcwd() can find the parent entry that names it. Both lines are asserted deliberately: the RBF line is the control, and matching only a bare PASS would let a harness that quietly stopped exercising RBF report a green result. Before the pDopt fix the host-native line read FAIL pdfd=00000000 -- directories shared the constant RBF option table, so PD_FD was always 0 -- which is what the ported bash reported as 'getwd: cannot access parent directories'.

RBF's automatic record locking (Read-in-UPDATE-mode locks the record just read; the following Write on that path releases it) makes a database-style read-modify-write race-safe under two concurrent racers with ZERO explicit application-level locking calls. Two racers x 300 increments each must land on exactly 600, no lost updates. Runs against a fresh RAM disk (mount -r), not the original dogfood pass's /h1/CLAUDETEST -- record locking is confirmed to work identically there (this suite must never touch the shared /h1 image).
